issues.description: The solution's PersonService.addChild method declares its parameters with reversed local names compared to the template and the problem statement description. The problem statement and template describe/declare the method as addChild(Person person, Person child) (i.e., first param is the parent, second is the child). In the solution the method is implemented as addChild(Person child, Person person) (the two parameters are still of the same type, so the code compiles and works, but the swapped parameter names conflict with the documented/templated ordering and may confuse students when they compare their implementation to the provided solution or when they rely on parameter names for understanding which argument represents the parent vs. the child.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter names and order consistent across artifacts. Change the solution method signature to public Person addChild(Person person, Person child) (and adjust the implementation variable names accordingly), so it matches the template and the problem statement's description. This preserves functionality while removing potential confusion.
